# rpc-project

> Simple RPC service for controlling every aspect of a remote machine — a C server and a Python client.

rpc-project: a C server and Python rpcclient for calling native functions and controlling a remote machine (filesystem, processes, network, HID, ObjC, and more).

# Getting started

# rpc-project

`rpc-project` is a simple, powerful **RPC service for controlling every aspect of a remote machine**. A small C **server** exposes a protocol for calling native functions; a Python **client** turns that into a rich, scriptable API. Use it for QA automation, for testing your APIs straight from Python, and for software research: found an interesting OS API? Try it with no compilation required.

## How it fits together

**Your machine**

`rpcclient`, written in Python 3. An IPython shell (or a library) that builds high-level APIs on top of native calls.

call → result

**The target**

`rpcserver`, a small binary written in C that exposes a protocol for calling native C functions. Runs on macOS, iOS and Linux.

## What you can reach

Each platform adds to the one around it: everything that works everywhere also works on Darwin, and everything on Darwin also works on iOS.

Every platform

- Remote system commands: `p.spawn()`
- Remote shell: `p.shell()`
- Filesystem: `p.fs.*`
- Network (Wi-Fi scan, TCP connect, …): `p.network.*`
- Sysctl: `p.sysctl.*`

Darwin (macOS and iOS)

- Multimedia record and play: `p.media.*`
- Preferences (CFPreferences, SCPreferences): `p.preferences.*`
- Process management: `p.processes.*`
- Location: `p.location.*`
- HID simulation (touch, keyboard, battery): `p.hid.*`
- IORegistry: `p.ioregistry.*`
- Logs and crash reports: `p.reports.*`
- Time, Bluetooth, XPC: `p.time.*`, `p.bluetooth.*`, `p.xpc.*`

iOS only

- MobileGestalt: `p.mobile_gestalt.*`
- Backlight: `p.backlight.*`
- Dump decrypted apps: `p.processes.get_by_basename(name).dump_app('/path')`

## Where to go next

[**Installation**\
Get the server binary and `pip install rpcclient`.](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/installation/index.md)

[**Quick start**\
Run the server and open the client shell.](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/quickstart/index.md)

[**API reference**\
The generated `rpcclient` reference.](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/index.md)

# Installation

## Client

Install the latest client from PyPI (requires **Python 3.10+**):

```
python3 -m pip install -U rpcclient
```

This provides two console entry points:

- `rpcclient [HOSTNAME]` — connect to a remote `rpcserver`
- `rpclocal` — control the **local** machine, no remote server required

## Server

Download and run the latest server artifact for your platform/arch from the latest [server-publish GitHub Action](https://github.com/doronz88/rpc-project/actions/workflows/server-publish.yml), or build it yourself (below).

## Building the server

Note

Cross-platform builds are not currently supported — build on the target OS.

Requires Xcode.

```
brew install protobuf protobuf-c
python3 -m pip install mypy-protobuf protobuf grpcio-tools
git clone git@github.com:doronz88/rpc-project.git
cd rpc-project
make -C src/protos/ all
cd src/rpcserver
mkdir build && cd build
cmake .. -DTARGET=OSX && make     # macOS
cmake .. -DTARGET=IOS && make     # iOS
```

```
sudo apt-get install -y protobuf-compiler libprotobuf-dev libprotoc-dev protobuf-c-compiler
python3 -m pip install mypy-protobuf protobuf grpcio-tools
git clone git@github.com:doronz88/rpc-project.git --recurse-submodules
cd rpc-project
make -C src/protos/ all
cd src/rpcserver
mkdir build && cd build
cmake .. -DTARGET=LINUX && make
```
# Guides

# Quick start

## Run the server

```
Usage: ./rpcserver [-p port] [-o (stdout|syslog|file:filename)]
-h  show this help message
-o  output. can be all of: stdout, syslog and file:filename. can be passed multiple times

Example:
./rpcserver -p 5910 -o syslog -o stdout -o file:/tmp/log.txt
```

## Connect the client

Connect to a running server (`HOSTNAME` is optional — omit it to start without a connection and connect later from the console):

```
rpcclient [HOSTNAME]
# or: python3 -m rpcclient [HOSTNAME]
```

To control the **local** machine (no remote server needed), use:

```
rpclocal
```

Full usage:

```
Usage: rpcclient [OPTIONS] [HOSTNAME]

  Start the console. If HOSTNAME is provided, connect immediately. Otherwise,
  start without a connection. You can connect later from the console.

Options:
  -p, --port INTEGER        TCP port to connect to
  -r, --rebind-symbols      reload all symbols upon connection
  -l, --load-all-libraries  load all libraries
  -f, --startup-files PATH  File(s) (python) to run on session start. Repeatable.
  --help                    Show this message and exit.
```

Connecting to a jailbroken iOS device

You'll need a TCP tunnel to the device first, e.g. with [pymobiledevice3](https://github.com/doronz88/pymobiledevice3):

```
python3 -m pymobiledevice3 usbmux forward 5910 5910 -vvv
```

## The console: `mgr`, `console`, `p`

You land in an IPython shell with three globals:

- **`mgr`** — client manager: `mgr.create(hostname="127.0.0.1", port=5910)`, `mgr.get(pid)`, `mgr.remove(pid)`, `mgr.clients`, `mgr.clear()`
- **`console`** — context controller: `console.switch(pid)`, or `console.switch()` to pick interactively
- **`p`** — the active client; auto-updated when you switch context (`p.info()`, `p.pid()`, `p.fs.listdir(".")`, `p.spawn([...])`)

`F1` shows help, `F2` shows active contexts, `F3` switches to the previous context, `F4` toggles auto-switch on creation.

```
[Rpc-client]: mgr.create(hostname="127.0.0.1")
Auto-switched to new client PID: 79669
[osx| (79669) rpcserver_macosx]: <MacosClient: 79669 | rpcserver_macosx>
```

## Try it

```
[osx| (78479) rpcserver_macosx]: p.spawn(['sleep', '1'])
SpawnResult(error=0, pid=25047, stdout=<_io.TextIOWrapper ...>)

[osx| (78479) rpcserver_macosx]: p.fs.listdir('.')
['common.c', 'Makefile', 'rpcserver.c', ...]

[osx| (78479) rpcserver_macosx]: p.processes.get_self().fds()
[FileFd(fd=0, path='/dev/ttys000'), ...]
```

Explore the rest through `p`. Next: [Calling native functions](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/calling-native-functions/index.md).

# Calling native functions

The core power of `rpcclient` is calling native functions and working with raw memory through `Symbol` objects.

```
s = p.symbol(0x12345678)

# Symbol extends `int`
assert isinstance(s, int)

# write into this memory
s.poke(b'abc')

# peek (read) 20 bytes of memory
print(s.peek(20))

# jump to `s` as a function, passing (1, "string") as its args
s(1, "string")

# change the item size used for derefs
s.item_size = 1
s[0] = 1            # *(char *)s = 1
s[1] = 1            # *(((char *)s)+1) = 1

# Symbol inherits from int, so all int operations apply
s += 4

# back to 8 to store pointers
s.item_size = 8
s[0] = 1            # *(intptr_t *)s = 1

# calling a symbol returns a symbol
s[0] = p.symbol(0x11223344)()

# which file is this address loaded from?
print(p.symbol(0x11223344).filename)
```

## Globalized symbols

Symbols already mapped into the running process are reachable through `symbols.<name>`. `symbols` is a `SymbolsJar` — a `dict` wrapper over all exported symbols:

```
x = symbols.malloc(20)
```

You can also use the bare name; the client checks for collisions and resolves it lazily:

```
x = malloc(20)
# equivalent to:
malloc = symbols.malloc
x = malloc(20)
```

## ObjC support

On Darwin systems, the built-in Objective-C support is often easier:

```
# create CF/NS objects with cf()
some_cf_string = p.cf('some string')

# create a new NSMutableDictionary
a = NSMutableDictionary.new()
print(NSMutableDictionary.bundle_path)            # where the class is loaded from
a = p.objc_get_class('NSMutableDictionary').new() # the long form

# each darwin object is a DarwinSymbol with objc_call(...)
a.objc_call('setObject:forKey:', p.cf('value'), p.cf('key'))
a.cfdesc                                           # CFDescription

# convert to an ObjectiveCSymbol for richer introspection
a = a.objc_symbol
a.show()                                           # classes/objects properties
a.setObject_forKey_(p.cf('value2'), p.cf('key2'))  # auto-completed selectors

# back to native python (via plistlib; plist-serializable objects only)
a = a.py()

# load all frameworks for ObjC auto-completion (same as client -l -r)
p.load_all_libraries()
```

### Autorelease pools

```
# create an autorelease pool context, drained at the end
pool_ctx = p.create_autorelease_pool_ctx()
# ... do stuff ...
pool_ctx.drain()

# same, as a context manager
with p.create_autorelease_pool_ctx() as pool_ctx:
    ...  # do stuff

# iterate over all currently existing autorelease pools and their objects
for pool in p.get_autorelease_pools():
    for obj in pool:
        ...  # do stuff with objects
```

### Run loop and threading

On Apple targets the server pumps the main thread's run loop for the lifetime of the connection and serves your requests on a dedicated thread. Anything driven by the main run loop or the main dispatch queue - blocks dispatched to the main queue, run loop timers and sources, framework callbacks and notifications - keeps making progress while you work:

```
main_run_loop = p.symbols.CFRunLoopGetMain()
# the main run loop is up and waiting for work, not blocked serving you
p.symbols.CFRunLoopIsWaiting(main_run_loop)
```

There is no need to run a loop yourself; calling `CFRunLoopRun()` over RPC only hangs your own session, since it never returns.

Note that requests are served off the main thread. APIs that must run on the main thread need to be dispatched there explicitly.

# Filesystem

The `fs` subsystem (`p.fs`) works with the target's filesystem: listing and walking directories, reading and writing files, copying files between your machine and the target, and changing permissions, ownership and links. On Darwin targets it also covers extended attributes, file flags and `statfs`.

Console vs. scripts

The examples below are written for the interactive console, where `smart_await` awaits each call for you. A console cell that already uses `await`, `async with` or `async for` is left as-is, so every call inside such a cell needs an explicit `await`. In scripts, `await` each call yourself - see [Scripting with rpcclient](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/scripting/index.md).

## Listing and walking directories

```
p.fs.listdir('/var/mobile/Library/Preferences')     # list of names, without '.' and '..'
p.fs.pwd()
p.fs.chdir('/var/mobile')
```

`scandir()` returns `DirEntry` objects. `name` and `path` are plain properties; `is_dir()`, `is_file()`, `is_symlink()` and `stat()` are calls:

```
entries = p.fs.scandir('/var/mobile/Library')
entry = entries[0]
entry.name, entry.path
entry.is_dir()
```

`walk()` mirrors `os.walk()` and `find()` yields every path under a directory. Both are async generators, so iterate them with `async for` (pass `topdown=False` for a bottom-up traversal):

```
async for root, dirs, files in p.fs.walk('/var/mobile/Library/Preferences'):
    print(root, len(files))

paths = [path async for path in p.fs.find('/tmp/logs')]
```

## Reading and writing files

For whole files, use `p.fs.write_file('/tmp/hello.txt', b'hello')` and `p.fs.read_file('/tmp/hello.txt')`.

`open(path, mode, access=0o777)` returns a remote `File` wrapping the target's file descriptor. `mode` is one of `'r'`, `'r+'` (read/write, must exist), `'rw'` (read/write, create and truncate), `'w'` (write-only, create and truncate) or `'w+'` (read/write, create, no truncate). Use it as an async context manager so the descriptor is closed:

```
async with await p.fs.open('/tmp/hello.txt', 'r') as f:
    header = await f.read(4)
    rest = await f.read()
```

Outside a context manager, close it with `deallocate()`:

```
f = p.fs.open('/tmp/data.bin', 'w+')
f.write(b'\x00' * 16)
f.pwrite(b'ABCD', 8)                                 # write at offset 8
f.pread(4, 8)                                        # b'ABCD'
f.seek(0, 2)                                         # SEEK_END; returns the new offset
f.fsync()
f.deallocate()
```

`File` also provides `tell()`, `fdatasync()`, `flock(operation)` (with `LOCK_*` from `rpcclient.core.structs.consts`), `dup()` and `parse(struct)` to read and parse a `construct` struct.

## Copying between your machine and the target

`push()` copies local files to the target and `pull()` copies remote files to your machine. Both accept a single path or a list, and `~` is expanded on each side:

```
p.fs.push('~/Desktop/config.plist', '/var/mobile/Documents/config.plist')
p.fs.pull('/var/mobile/Library/Preferences/com.apple.springboard.plist', '/tmp/')
p.fs.pull('/var/mobile/Media/DCIM', '/tmp/dcim', recursive=True)
```

Directories are skipped unless `recursive=True`; a copied directory lands inside the destination as `<dest>/<name>`. Existing destination files are **not** overwritten unless you pass `force=True`.

To edit a remote file with local tools, `remote_file()` pulls it into a local temporary directory, yields the local `Path`, and pushes it back (with `force=True`) when the block exits:

```
async with p.fs.remote_file('/var/mobile/Library/Preferences/com.example.app.plist') as local:
    data = local.read_bytes()
    local.write_bytes(data.replace(b'old', b'new'))
```

## Stat, permissions and ownership

```
st = p.fs.stat('/var/mobile/Documents/notes.txt')    # follows symlinks
st.st_size, oct(st.st_mode), st.st_uid, st.st_mtime
p.fs.lstat('/var/mobile/Documents/link')             # does not follow symlinks
p.fs.is_file('/var/mobile/Documents/notes.txt')
p.fs.accessible('/var/root')                         # access(path, R_OK) == 0
p.fs.realpath('/tmp/../var/mobile')
```

`chmod()` and `chown()` take an optional `recursive=True`, which applies the change to every path under a directory. Pass `-1` to `chown()` to leave the uid or gid unchanged:

```
p.fs.chmod('/tmp/tool', 0o755)
p.fs.chown('/var/mobile/Documents/export', 501, 501, recursive=True)
p.fs.chown('/tmp/tool', 0, -1)
```

## Creating, removing and renaming

```
p.fs.mkdir('/tmp/work/a/b', parents=True)
p.fs.mkdir('/tmp/work', exist_ok=True)
p.fs.touch('/tmp/work/empty.txt')                    # mode=0o666, exist_ok=True
p.fs.rename('/tmp/work/empty.txt', '/tmp/work/a/empty.txt')
p.fs.remove('/tmp/work/a/empty.txt')
p.fs.remove('/tmp/work', recursive=True)             # force=True ignores errors
```

For scratch space, `remote_temp_dir()` creates a uniquely named directory (under `/tmp` by default) and removes it with its contents when the block exits:

```
async with await p.fs.remote_temp_dir() as tmp:
    await (tmp / 'out.bin').write_bytes(b'data')
```

## Links

```
p.fs.symlink('/var/mobile/Documents/notes.txt', '/tmp/notes')   # symlink(target, link)
p.fs.link('/tmp/hello.txt', '/tmp/hello-hardlink.txt')         # hard link
p.fs.is_symlink('/tmp/notes')
p.fs.readlink('/tmp/notes')                    # resolved against the link's directory
p.fs.readlink('/tmp/notes', absolute=False)    # the raw link contents
```

## Remote paths

`remote_path()` returns a `RemotePath`, a `PurePosixPath` bound to the client. Path arithmetic is local; filesystem methods such as `exists()`, `is_dir()`, `stat()`, `read_bytes()`, `write_bytes()`, `mkdir()`, `touch()`, `remove()` and `chmod()` run on the target. Any `fs` method accepts a `RemotePath` wherever it takes a path.

```
docs = p.fs.remote_path('/var/mobile/Documents')
notes = docs / 'notes.txt'
notes.exists()
notes.read_bytes()
names = [child.name async for child in docs.iterdir()]
```

## Darwin: extended attributes, flags and statfs

```
path = '/var/mobile/Downloads/app.zip'
p.fs.listxattr(path)                                 # ['com.apple.quarantine', ...]
p.fs.getxattr(path, 'com.apple.quarantine')          # bytes
p.fs.dictxattr(path)                                 # {name: bytes}
p.fs.setxattr(path, 'com.example.tag', b'value')
p.fs.removexattr(path, 'com.apple.quarantine')
```

`chflags()` sets BSD file flags, with constants from `rpcclient.clients.darwin.consts`:

```
from rpcclient.clients.darwin.consts import UF_IMMUTABLE

p.fs.chflags('/tmp/locked.txt', UF_IMMUTABLE)        # remove() now fails with RpcPermissionError
p.fs.chflags('/tmp/locked.txt', 0)
```

`statfs()` describes the volume a path lives on:

```
vfs = p.fs.statfs('/var/mobile')
vfs.f_mntonname, vfs.f_fstypename, vfs.f_bavail * vfs.f_bsize
```

See also: [Core API reference](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/core/index.md), [Darwin API reference](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/darwin/#filesystem), [Mounting in Finder (WebDAV)](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/mounting-webdav/index.md).

# Processes

`p.spawn()` runs commands on the remote host. The `processes` subsystem (`p.processes`) lists the running processes and returns `Process` objects that let you inspect another process, read and write its memory, and signal it. The base client only provides `kill()` and `waitpid()`. Everything else on this page needs a Darwin (macOS/iOS) client.

Note

The examples use the interactive console, where calls are awaited automatically. In a script, `await` each call (`proc = await p.processes.get_by_pid(1)`). See [Scripting](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/scripting/index.md).

## Running commands with spawn

`spawn()` runs `argv` with `envp` and forwards the process's stdin and stdout/stderr. By default it runs `/bin/sh` attached to your terminal, so `p.spawn()` gives you an interactive remote shell:

```
p.spawn()                                   # interactive /bin/sh
p.spawn(['/bin/ls', '-la', '/'])            # output goes to sys.stdout
```

It returns a `SpawnResult(error, pid, stdout)`. `stdin` takes a file object or a string to feed to the process, and `stdout` takes any file object that should receive both stdout and stderr:

```
from io import StringIO

out = StringIO()
result = p.spawn(['/bin/echo', 'hello'], stdin='', stdout=out)
result.error                # 0 on success
out.getvalue()              # 'hello\n'
```

Pass `raw_tty=True` to put your local terminal in raw mode for the session, which helps with full-screen programs. With `background=True`, `spawn()` returns as soon as the process starts, and `error` and `stdout` are `None`:

```
result = p.spawn(['/bin/sleep', '60'], stdout=StringIO(), stdin='', background=True)
p.processes.kill(result.pid)
```

## Finding processes

```
p.processes.list()                       # every running process, as Process objects
p.processes.get_self()                   # the rpcserver process itself
p.processes.get_by_pid(1)                # raises ArgumentError if no such pid
p.processes.get_by_basename('launchd')   # exact match on the executable's file name
p.processes.get_by_name('launchd')       # exact match on the kernel's process name (pbi_name)
p.processes.grep('Spring')               # every process whose basename contains the string
```

You can also look processes up by what they have open:

```
p.processes.get_processes_by_listening_port(5910)   # processes with a socket listening on the port
p.processes.fuser('/var/log/system.log')            # processes with the file open
p.processes.lsof()                                  # {pid: [Fd, ...]} for every process you can read
```

## Inspecting a process

Keep the `Process` in a variable. `pid` is a plain property. Everything else is a method, so call it:

```
proc = p.processes.get_by_basename('launchd')
proc.pid                 # 1
proc.path()              # '/sbin/launchd'
proc.basename()          # 'launchd'
proc.name()
proc.bundle_id()         # code-signing identity, e.g. 'com.apple.Preferences'; None if unsigned
proc.ppid(), proc.uid(), proc.gid(), proc.ruid(), proc.rgid()
proc.parent()            # the parent as a Process
proc.start_time()        # datetime (arm64 only)
proc.arguments()         # ['/sbin/launchd']
proc.environ()           # {'PATH': '...', ...}
proc.cdhash()            # bytes
```

`task_all_info()`, `task_vm_info()` and `procargs2()` return the raw parsed kernel structures.

### File descriptors

`fds()` returns a list of `Fd` dataclasses. The subclass tells you the descriptor type: `FileFd` and `UnixFd` (with `path`), `SharedMemoryFd`, `PipeFd`, `KQueueFd`, and `Ipv4TcpFd`, `Ipv6TcpFd`, `Ipv4UdpFd` and `Ipv6UdpFd` (with `local_address`, `local_port`, `remote_address`, `remote_port`):

```
proc = p.processes.get_self()
proc.fds()
[FileFd(fd=0, path='/dev/ttys000'), FileFd(fd=1, path='/dev/ttys000'), ...]
```

### Images, regions and classes

```
proc.images()            # [Image(address=..., path='/usr/lib/dyld'), ...]
proc.app_images()        # only the images inside the .app bundle
proc.regions()           # [Region(region_type=..., start=..., end=..., protection='r-x', ...), ...]
```

Each `Region` has `start`, `end`, `size`, `protection`, `protection_max`, `region_type` and `region_detail`. `loaded_classes()` is an async generator over the Objective-C classes realized in the process, so loop over it with `async for`. A cell that contains `async for` is not rewritten by the console, so `await` any calls inside it yourself:

```
async for cls in proc.loaded_classes():
    print(cls.name, cls.binary_path)
```

### Threads and backtraces

```
threads = proc.threads()         # [ArmThread64 / IntelThread64, ...]
t = threads[0]
t.thread_id
t.get_state()                    # parsed register state
t.suspend()
t.resume()
proc.backtraces()                # one Backtrace (with frames) per thread
```

`t.set_state(state)` writes a register state built from a dict that has the same fields as `get_state()`.

### Symbols, Mach ports and memory graphs

```
proc.get_symbol_address('malloc', 'libsystem_malloc.dylib')
proc.get_symbol_image('malloc')  # the Image that exports it
proc.get_memgraph_snapshot()     # memory graph as plist bytes
```

`get_mach_ports()` is an async generator of `MachPortInfo` entries (`name`, `rights`, `kobject`, `exception`, ...). `get_mach_port_cross_ref_info()` shows which process holds the receive right for each of this process's ports. It only sees other tasks' ports when `rpcserver` runs as root.

```
async for port in proc.get_mach_ports(resolve_kobjects=True):
    print(port.name, port.rights, port.kobject)
```

`proc.preferences()` reads and writes the preference domain the way this process resolves it (its own container and uid), for example `proc.preferences().get_dict()`.

## Reading and writing another process's memory

`peek()`, `peek_str()` and `poke()` take an address in the target process. Addresses that come back from `images()`, `regions()` and `vm_allocate()` are `ProcessSymbol` objects. A `ProcessSymbol` is an `int` bound to its process, so you can do arithmetic on it and call `peek()`/`poke()` on it directly:

```
proc = p.processes.get_by_basename('Finder')
base = proc.images()[0].address
proc.peek(base, 4)               # b'\xcf\xfa\xed\xfe'
base.peek(4)                     # the same, through the ProcessSymbol
(base + 0x10).peek(8)

buf = proc.vm_allocate(0x1000)   # allocate memory in the target
buf.poke(b'hello\x00')
buf.peek_str()                   # 'hello'
proc.get_process_symbol(0x100000000)   # wrap any address of the target
```

A `ProcessSymbol` cannot be called. To run code, use a client connected to that process.

Note

Reads use `task_read_for_pid()`, while writes and `vm_allocate()` use `task_for_pid()`. To work on other processes, `rpcserver` must run as root and carry the `task_for_pid-allow` entitlement (included in `ents.plist`). Hardened or platform processes may still refuse.

## Signals and waiting

```
from rpcclient.core.structs.consts import SIGKILL

proc.kill()                      # SIGTERM by default
proc.kill(SIGKILL)
p.processes.kill(1234, SIGKILL)  # by pid
p.processes.waitpid(result.pid)  # exit status; only for children of rpcserver, such as spawned ones
```

`p.processes.disable_watchdog()` kills `watchdogd` once a second in a loop that never returns.

## iOS: launching and dumping apps

On iOS, `launch()` starts an app through BackBoardServices and returns its `Process`. By default it kills any running instance first. It can also disable ASLR, wait for a debugger, or redirect stdout/stderr to a file on the device. It raises `LaunchError` if the app does not start:

```
proc = p.processes.launch('com.apple.calculator')
proc = p.processes.launch('com.example.app', disable_aslr=True, wait_for_debugger=True,
                          stdout='/tmp/app.out', stderr='/tmp/app.err')
```

`dump_app(output_dir)` writes each Mach-O in the app bundle to a local directory, keeping its path relative to the `.app`. For encrypted binaries it copies the decrypted pages from memory and sets `cryptid` to 0, in the same way as frida-ios-dump. Launch the app first so its images are loaded:

```
proc = p.processes.launch('com.example.app')
proc.dump_app('~/dumps/example')
```

See also: [Darwin API](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/darwin/#processes), [iOS API](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/ios/index.md), [Calling native functions](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/calling-native-functions/index.md).

# Networking

The `network` subsystem (`p.network`) does networking from the target's side: it lists the target's interfaces, resolves host names with the target's resolver and opens TCP and Unix-domain connections from the target process. On Darwin clients it also reads and sets the system proxy and can remove certificate pinning. On iOS, `p.wifi` controls the Wi-Fi radio. The mDNSResponder cache has its own guide: [DNS cache](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/dns/index.md).

Note

The examples are written for the interactive console, where calls are awaited for you. In a script, `await` each call (see [Scripting with rpcclient](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/scripting/index.md)). `async with` is needed in both.

## Listing interfaces

`interfaces()` returns the IPv4 interfaces of the target as `Interface(name, address, netmask, broadcast)` named tuples. Interfaces without an IPv4 address are left out, and `broadcast` is `None` when there isn't one:

```
for iface in p.network.interfaces():
    print(iface.name, iface.address, iface.netmask, iface.broadcast)
```

## Resolving host names

`gethostbyname()` resolves a name on the target and returns `Hostentry(name, aliases, addresses)`, or `None` if the name doesn't resolve. `addresses` holds IPv4 addresses as strings:

```
entry = p.network.gethostbyname("apple.com")
entry.addresses
p.network.gethostbyname("no-such-host.invalid")   # None
```

## Connecting from the target

`tcp_connect(address, port)` makes the target connect to `address:port` and returns a `Socket`. The address must be an IPv4 or IPv6 literal (anything containing `:` is treated as IPv6), so resolve names first. `unix_connect(path)` does the same for a Unix-domain socket on the target. A `Socket` is an async context manager that closes the remote file descriptor on exit:

```
async with await p.network.tcp_connect("127.0.0.1", 8080) as sock:
    await sock.sendall(b"GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n")
    print(await sock.recv(1024))

async with await p.network.unix_connect("/var/run/mDNSResponder") as sock:
    ...
```

Inside an `async with` block the console doesn't await for you, hence the explicit `await`s. Outside one, assign the socket and close it yourself:

```
sock = p.network.tcp_connect("127.0.0.1", 8080)
sock.sendall(b"ping")
sock.recvall(4)        # block until exactly 4 bytes arrive
sock.deallocate()      # close the fd
```

A refused connection raises `RpcConnectionRefusedError`, and a missing Unix socket path raises `RpcFileNotFoundError`.

The `Socket` methods are:

- `send(buf, size=None, flags=0)` sends once and returns the number of bytes sent; `sendall(buf)` keeps sending until the whole buffer is written. `MSG_NOSIGNAL` is always added to the flags.
- `recv(size=1024, flags=0)` returns up to `size` bytes; `recvall(size)` waits for exactly `size` bytes. Both raise if the peer closes the connection.
- `settimeout(seconds)` sets `SO_RCVTIMEO`/`SO_SNDTIMEO`; a timed-out `recv()` raises `RpcResourceTemporarilyUnavailableError`. `gettimeout()` returns the value last set.
- `setblocking(flag)`, `getblocking()`, `setbufsize(size)` and `setsockopt(level, option_name, option_value)` wrap `fcntl()` and `setsockopt()`.
- `fd` is the remote file descriptor.

There are no helpers for UDP or for listening. `p.network.socket(family, socktype, proto)` creates a socket and returns its raw file descriptor, which you can drive with `bind()`, `listen()`, `sendto()` and so on through `p.symbols` (see [Calling native functions](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/calling-native-functions/index.md)).

## Proxies and certificate pinning (Darwin)

```
p.network.proxy_settings()                    # CFNetworkCopySystemProxySettings() as a dict
p.network.set_http_proxy("192.168.1.10", 8080)
p.network.remove_http_proxy()
```

`set_http_proxy()` writes an HTTP and HTTPS proxy into the managed SystemConfiguration preferences and `remove_http_proxy()` removes it. Both then kill `configd` so the change takes effect.

`remove_certificate_pinning()` empties trustd's pinning rules database (`/private/var/protected/trustd/pinningrules.sqlite3`) and restarts trustd. `restore_certificate_pinning()` deletes the database so trustd reloads the rules from its last MobileAsset on restart. `kill_trustd()` restarts trustd on its own, and `flush_dns()` restarts mDNSResponder.

These change system state and generally need `rpcserver` to run as root.

## Wi-Fi (iOS)

`p.wifi` turns Wi-Fi on and off, lists saved networks, and scans for and joins networks:

```
p.wifi.is_on()
p.wifi.turn_off()
p.wifi.turn_on()
p.wifi.interfaces()                 # e.g. ['en0']

for network in p.wifi.saved_networks():
    print(network.ssid(), network.bssid())
# network.forget() removes a saved network
```

Scanning and joining go through an interface handle from `get_interface()`, which uses the first Wi-Fi interface unless you pass a name. The handle is closed when the `async with` block exits:

```
async with await p.wifi.get_interface() as iface:
    networks = await iface.scan()
    for n in networks:
        print(n.ssid, n.bssid, n.rssi, n.channel)
    await networks[0].connect("password")   # omit the password for open networks
    await iface.disconnect()
```

Scanned networks expose `ssid` (bytes), `bssid`, `rssi` and `channel` as plain properties, and the raw scan dictionary as `network`. On saved networks, `ssid()` and `bssid()` are methods, and `get_property(name)` reads any other WiFiNetwork property.

See also: API reference for [Darwin](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/darwin/index.md) and [iOS](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/ios/index.md), and the [DNS cache](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/dns/index.md) guide.

# Using rpcclient from your own scripts

The `rpcclient` API is asynchronous: every call that talks to the server is a coroutine. The interactive console hides this (see [How the console differs](#how-the-console-differs)), which is why most examples in these guides have no `await`. In a normal Python program you run an event loop yourself and `await` each call.

## Connect to a server

Create clients through a `ClientManager`. It picks the right client class for the target (macOS, iOS, Linux) and keeps track of every client it created. The default transport is TCP:

```
from rpcclient.client_manager import ClientManager

manager = ClientManager()
client = await manager.create(hostname="127.0.0.1", port=5910)
```

`port` defaults to `5910`, and an optional `timeout` (in seconds) limits how long the connection attempt may take. A refused connection raises `rpcclient.exceptions.FailedToConnectError`.

To control the local machine without starting a server yourself, use the `local` transport. This is what `rpclocal` does:

```
client = await manager.create(mode="local")
```

It downloads the latest `rpcserver_macosx` release from GitHub into the current working directory, starts it on a free port and connects to it. Closing the client also stops that server process.

## A minimal script

```
import asyncio

from rpcclient.client_manager import ClientManager


async def main() -> None:
    client = await ClientManager().create(hostname="127.0.0.1")
    async with client:
        print(client)
        print("pid:", await client.get_pid())
        print("sysname:", (await client.get_uname()).sysname)
        print(await client.fs.listdir("/"))


asyncio.run(main())
```

Every method that reaches the server needs `await`, including subscript reads on symbols (`await s.getindex(0)` rather than `s[0]`) and context managers such as `async with client.safe_malloc(8) as buf:`.

## Closing the client

`await client.close()` tells the server to end the session and closes the socket. Clients are async context managers, so `async with client:` closes it for you, even when an exception is raised. This is the pattern the test suite uses:

```
async with await ClientManager().create(hostname="127.0.0.1") as client:
    ...
```

If you created several clients through one manager, `await manager.close_all()` closes all of them and empties `manager.clients`. Put it in a `finally` block:

```
manager = ClientManager()
try:
    client = await manager.create(hostname="127.0.0.1")
    ...
finally:
    await manager.close_all()
```

## Concurrent calls

A client can be shared between tasks. You can pass several of its calls to `asyncio.gather`:

```
pid, cwd, home = await asyncio.gather(
    client.symbols.getpid(),
    client.fs.pwd(),
    client.getenv("HOME"),
)
```

Requests on one client go over one socket, one at a time, so this is safe but does not make the server do the work in parallel. For real parallelism, open more clients. Each connection is served by its own server process:

```
a, b = await asyncio.gather(
    manager.create(hostname="127.0.0.1"),
    manager.create(hostname="127.0.0.1"),
)
listing_a, listing_b = await asyncio.gather(a.fs.listdir("/"), b.fs.listdir("/"))
```

## How the console differs

`rpcclient` and `rpclocal` start IPython with `autoawait` turned on, so top-level `await` works. They also load the `smart_await` extension, which rewrites each cell before it runs:

- a call that returns an awaitable is awaited: `p.get_pid()` gives an `int`
- a subscript read that returns an awaitable is awaited: `s[0]`
- a subscript assignment `s[0] = 7` becomes `await s.setindex(0, 7)` when `s` has an async `setindex`

To get the coroutine itself instead of its result, wrap the call in `...( )`, for example `task = ...(p.fs.listdir("/"))`.

`smart_await` leaves a cell untouched if the cell already uses `await` or another `async` construct. In a cell with `async with` or `async for`, which the console cannot add for you, write `await` on every call in that cell yourself.

## Startup files

`rpcclient -f FILE` (and `rpclocal -f FILE`) runs files in the console before the prompt appears, with `p`, `mgr` and `console` already defined. This is useful for setup that you then continue by hand. How the file runs depends on its extension:

- A `.ipy` file runs like typed console input, so console-style code without `await` works.
- A `.py` file runs as plain Python. Calls return coroutines, and top-level `await` is a syntax error. Run coroutines on the console's event loop with `run_in_loop`:

```
from rpcclient.utils import run_in_loop

pid = run_in_loop(p.get_pid())
```

Note

Use `run_in_loop` only in startup files and other synchronous code that shares the console's loop. In a standalone script, use `asyncio.run` and `await`.

See also: [Quick start](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/quickstart/index.md), [Core API](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/core/index.md).

# Mounting a remote path in Finder (WebDAV)

`rpcclient` can expose any path on the remote target as a local **WebDAV** volume, so macOS Finder (or any WebDAV client) can browse and edit the remote filesystem read-write as if it were mounted.

A small async WebDAV server runs **inside the `rpcclient` process**; every WebDAV request is translated into `client.fs` calls against the target. Nothing runs on the target and there are no server-side changes, so it works the same for iOS, macOS, and Linux targets.

WebDAV is used rather than FTP because macOS Finder mounts FTP **read-only** — it only allows writes to servers that implement WebDAV locking, which this server does.

## Quick start

Serve the target's root and mount it in your file manager in one step:

```
rpcdav HOSTNAME --mount
```

`--mount` uses the host's native WebDAV mechanism — `mount_webdav` on macOS, `net use` on Windows, `gio mount` on Linux — and reveals the volume in the file manager. If none is available, it falls back to printing the URL to open manually.

Serve a specific path instead of `/`:

```
rpcdav HOSTNAME /var/mobile/Containers --mount
```

The same is available as a subcommand of `rpcclient`:

```
rpcclient HOSTNAME webdav [PATH] [--mount]
```

Press `Ctrl-C` to unmount and stop the server.

## Mounting manually

Without `--mount`, the server prints its local URL:

```
WebDAV server serving '/' at http://127.0.0.1:52314/
In Finder: Go → Connect to Server → http://127.0.0.1:52314/
```

In Finder, choose **Go → Connect to Server** (`⌘K`) and enter that URL (on Linux/Windows, open it in your file manager's "connect to server" equivalent, or use any WebDAV client).

## Usage

```
Usage: rpcdav [OPTIONS] HOSTNAME [PATH]

  Serve a remote HOSTNAME's PATH (default: /) over WebDAV for local mounting.

Options:
  -p, --port INTEGER        TCP port to connect to
  -r, --rebind-symbols      reload all symbols upon connection
  -l, --load-all-libraries  load all libraries
  --mount                   mount the served path locally and reveal it in your file manager
  --host TEXT               local interface to bind
  --bind-port INTEGER       local TCP port (0 picks a free port)
  --readonly                expose the path read-only
```

## From a script

The `webdav` subsystem is available on every client:

```
server = await client.webdav.serve("/var/mobile", host="127.0.0.1", port=0)
print(server.url)  # http://127.0.0.1:<port>/
# ... use the mount ...
await server.stop()
```

## Notes and limitations

- **Freshness / stale views.** A mounted WebDAV volume is a *client-cached network filesystem*. Changes you make through the mount are immediate, but changes made on the target out-of-band may appear stale until the client revalidates. WebDAV has no live-reload mechanism, and macOS's WebDAV client caches directory listings and attributes at the kernel level regardless of server hints. To force a refresh, navigate out of the folder and back (or reopen the window).
- **Read-write** browse, read, create, edit, `mkdir`, rename/move, and delete all propagate to the target.
- **Finder metadata** (`.DS_Store`, AppleDouble `._*`, …) writes are swallowed — reported as success but never written to the target, so they don't clutter it or fail on read-only roots.
- **`chmod` / `chown` do not propagate.** WebDAV has no representation for POSIX permissions or ownership, and macOS's WebDAV client never sends them — such changes on the mount are local no-ops. Use `client.fs.chmod(...)` / `client.fs.chown(...)` for real remote permission changes.
- **New files and directories** are created by the process the `rpcserver` runs as, so they are owned by that user (e.g. `root` when the server runs as root), with the server's default permissions — not your local user.

# DNS cache

The `dns` subsystem (`p.dns`) works with mDNSResponder, the daemon behind all name resolution on macOS and iOS. It reads its DNS cache, injects records into it and flushes records out of it.

`rpcserver` must run as **root**, and `delete()` also needs it signed with the `com.apple.private.mDNSResponder.record-cache.flush` entitlement (included in `ents.plist`).

## Reading the cache

mDNSResponder only hands out its cache through a state dump, which recent OS versions disable for privacy. Enable it once per device (this persists across reboots and restarts mDNSResponder):

```
p.dns.enable_state_dump()
```

Then:

```
cache = p.dns.cache()
cache                        # prints as a table
cache.find("apple.com")      # the records of one name
for record in cache.records:
    print(record.name, record.type, record.ttl, record.rdata)
```

```
DNS cache: 57 records (77/146 entities in use, 9 unicast, 48 multicast, 4 referenced by active questions)

  NAME                         TYPE  TTL  IF      KIND     DNSSEC DATA
* _companion-link._tcp.local.  PTR   4270 en0     shared          user’s Mac mini._companion-link._tcp.local.
  time.apple.com.              CNAME 4367 unicast unique          time.g.aaplimg.com.
  dns.google.                  HTTPS 172  en0     negative        <no such record>
```

The full state dump (questions, resolvers, interfaces, statistics, ...) is available too:

```
dump = p.dns.state_dump()
dump.sections().keys()
print(dump.section("DNS Services"))
```

`p.dns.disable_state_dump()` turns it off again.

## Injecting records

`add()` registers a record that mDNSResponder answers with before consulting its cache or the network:

```
record = p.dns.add("printer.local", "192.168.1.50")          # A
p.dns.add("printer.local", "fe80::1", rrtype="AAAA", ttl=60)
p.dns.add("_http._tcp.example.com", ["path=/"], rrtype="TXT")
p.dns.update("printer.local", "192.168.1.51")                 # replace the A record
p.dns.records()                                                     # what this client injected
p.dns.remove(record)
p.dns.remove_all()
```

Address records are limited to local domains

mDNSResponder only accepts A, AAAA and CNAME records for names in the link-local domains: `local.`, `254.169.in-addr.arpa.` and `{8,9,a,b}.e.f.ip6.arpa.`. It refuses them for any other name, regardless of root or entitlements, so that a process can't redirect e.g. `www.bigbank.com`. `add()` raises `ArgumentError` for those. Other record types can be added for any name.

Injected records live as long as their connection to mDNSResponder: until they are removed, or until rpcserver or mDNSResponder exits.

## Flushing

```
p.dns.delete("example.com")   # injected and cached records of one name
p.dns.clear()                 # the whole cache, by restarting mDNSResponder
```

Records an active question references are re-resolved right away and may reappear, and Bonjour records are relearned as soon as mDNSResponder restarts.
# API reference

# API Reference

Generated from the `rpcclient` source. The client is organized as a per-platform `Client` built on a shared core, exposing subsystems as attributes (`p.fs`, `p.network`, `p.processes`, …).

- **[Core client](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/core/index.md)** — the abstract client, symbols, and exceptions.
- **[Platform clients](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/clients/index.md)** — Linux / macOS / Darwin / iOS clients.
- **[Darwin subsystems](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/darwin/index.md)** — filesystem, network, processes, HID, media, and more.
- **[iOS subsystems](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/api/ios/index.md)** — MobileGestalt, SpringBoard, lockdown, backlight, and more.

New here? Start with the [Quick start](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/quickstart/index.md) and [Calling native functions](https://doronz88.github.io/rpc-project/latest/guides/calling-native-functions/index.md) guides.

# Core client

## CoreClient

## rpcclient.core.client.CoreClient

Bases: `Generic[SymbolT_co]`, `ABC`

Main client interface to access the remote rpcserver

Source code in `src/rpcclient/rpcclient/core/client.py`

```
class CoreClient(Generic[SymbolT_co], abc.ABC):
    """Main client interface to access the remote rpcserver"""

    DEFAULT_ARGV: ClassVar[list[str]] = ["/bin/sh"]
    DEFAULT_ENVP: ClassVar[list[str]] = []

    def __init__(self, bridge: RpcBridge, dlsym_global_handle: int = RTLD_NEXT) -> None:
        self._bridge: RpcBridge = bridge
        self._old_settings = None
        self._endianness: Literal["<", ">"] = "<"
        self._dlsym_global_handle: int = dlsym_global_handle
        self._logger: logging.Logger = logging.getLogger(self.__module__)
        self.notifier: EventNotifier = EventNotifier()
        self.pre_rpc_call_hooks: list[Callable[[], Coroutine[Any, Any, object]]] = []
        self._protocol_lock: asyncio.Lock = asyncio.Lock()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def _acquire_protocol_lock(self) -> AsyncGenerator[None]:
        async with self._protocol_lock:
            yield

    @cached_property
    def symbols(self) -> SymbolsJar[SymbolT_co]:
        return SymbolsJar(self)

    @cached_property
    def null(self) -> SymbolT_co:
        return self.symbol(0)

    @classmethod
    async def create(cls, bridge: RpcBridge) -> Self:
        return cls(bridge)

    @subsystem
    @abc.abstractmethod
    def fs(self) -> Fs[Self]: ...

    @subsystem
    def processes(self) -> Processes[Self]:
        return Processes(self)

    @subsystem
    def network(self) -> Network[Self]:
        return Network(self)

    @subsystem
    def lief(self) -> Lief[Self]:
        return Lief(self)

    @subsystem
    def sysctl(self) -> Sysctl[Self]:
        return Sysctl(self)

    @subsystem
    def webdav(self) -> WebDav[Self]:
        return WebDav(self)

    async def info(self) -> None:
        """print information about the current target"""
        uname = await self.get_uname()
        print("sysname:", uname.sysname)
        print("nodename:", uname.nodename)
        print("release:", uname.release)
        print("version:", uname.version)
        print("machine:", uname.machine)
        print(f"uid: {(await self.symbols.getuid()):d}")
        print(f"gid: {(await self.symbols.getgid()):d}")
        print(f"pid: {await self.get_pid():d}")
        print(f"ppid: {(await self.symbols.getppid()):d}")
        print(f"progname: {await self.get_progname()}")

    _cached_progname: str | None = None

    async def get_progname(self) -> str:
        """get the program name from remote"""
        if self._cached_progname is None:
            # bugfix https://github.com/doronz88/rpc-project/issues/405
            # Default Linux libraries don't expose `getprogname()`, so instead we use the `__progname` global symbol.
            # Tested on both macOS and Ubuntu.
            self._cached_progname = await (await self.symbols["__progname"].getindex(0)).peek_str()

        return self._cached_progname

    async def progname(self) -> str:
        """get the program name from remote"""
        return await self.get_progname()

    @abc.abstractmethod
    async def get_uname(self) -> Container:
        """get the utsname struct from remote"""

    async def uname(self) -> Container:
        """get the utsname struct from remote"""
        return await self.get_uname()

    @property
    def id(self) -> int:
        return self._bridge.client_id

    @property
    def platform(self) -> str:
        return self._bridge.platform

    @property
    def sysname(self) -> str:
        return self._bridge.sysname

    @property
    def arch(self) -> int:
        return self._bridge.arch

    async def rpc_call(self, msg_id: int, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        # Pop all hooks here, to prevent hooks from running out of order due to recursion.
        hooks, self.pre_rpc_call_hooks[:] = self.pre_rpc_call_hooks[::-1], []
        try:
            while hooks:
                await hooks.pop()()
        finally:
            # In case of failure, re-insert the remaining hooks.
            if hooks:
                self.pre_rpc_call_hooks[:0] = hooks

        try:
            return await self._bridge.rpc_call(msg_id, **kwargs)
        except ConnectionError:
            self.notifier.notify(ClientEvent.TERMINATED, self.id)
            self._bridge.close()
            raise
        except ServerResponseError:
            raise

    async def dlopen(self, filename: str, mode: int) -> SymbolT_co:
        """Load a shared library on the remote host and return its handle."""
        return self.symbol((await self.rpc_call(MsgId.REQ_DLOPEN, filename=filename, mode=mode)).handle)

    async def dlclose(self, lib: int) -> int:
        """Close a previously opened remote library handle."""
        return (await self.rpc_call(MsgId.REQ_DLCLOSE, handle=ctypes.c_uint64(lib).value)).res

    async def dlsym(self, lib: int, symbol_name: str) -> int:
        """Resolve a symbol name in a remote library handle and return its address.

        Runs and pops any hooks in `self.pre_dlsym_hooks` first.
        """
        return (await self.rpc_call(MsgId.REQ_DLSYM, handle=ctypes.c_uint64(lib).value, symbol_name=symbol_name)).ptr

    @null_pointer_guard
    async def call(
        self,
        address: int,
        argv: Iterable[RemoteCallArg] = (),
        return_float64: bool = False,
        return_float32: bool = False,
        return_raw: bool = False,
        va_list_index: int | None = None,
    ) -> float | SymbolT_co | Any:
        """call a remote function and retrieve its return value as a Symbol object"""
        if va_list_index is None:
            va_list_index = 0xFFFF

        args: list[Argument] = []
        for arg in argv:
            if isinstance(arg, LazySymbol):
                arg = int(await arg.resolve())

            if isinstance(arg, float):
                args.append(Argument(v_double=arg))
            elif isinstance(arg, str):
                args.append(Argument(v_str=arg))
            elif isinstance(arg, int):
                args.append(Argument(v_int=ctypes.c_uint64(arg).value))
            elif isinstance(arg, bytes):
                args.append(Argument(v_bytes=arg))
            elif isinstance(arg, Enum):
                args.append(Argument(v_int=ctypes.c_uint64(arg.value).value))
            elif isinstance(arg, PurePath):
                args.append(Argument(v_str=str(arg)))
            else:
                assert_never(arg)
                raise ArgumentError(f"Can't serialize object of type {type(arg).__name__}")

        ret = await self.rpc_call(MsgId.REQ_CALL, address=address, va_list_index=va_list_index, argv=args)
        if ret.HasField("arm_registers"):
            d0 = ret.arm_registers.d0
            if return_float32:
                return ctypes.c_float(d0).value
            if return_float64:
                return d0
            if return_raw:
                return ret.arm_registers
            return self.symbol(ret.arm_registers.x0)
        return self.symbol(ret.return_value)

    @null_pointer_guard
    async def peek(self, address: int, size: int) -> bytes:
        """peek data at the given address"""
        try:
            return (await self.rpc_call(MsgId.REQ_PEEK, address=address, size=size)).data
        except ServerResponseError as e:
            raise ArgumentError() from e

    @null_pointer_guard
    async def poke(self, address: int, data: bytes) -> Any:
        """poke data at a given address"""
        try:
            return await self.rpc_call(MsgId.REQ_POKE, address=address, data=data)
        except ServerResponseError as e:
            raise ArgumentError() from e

    async def get_dummy_block(self) -> SymbolT_co:
        """Get an address for a stub block containing nothing"""
        block_size = block_literal.sizeof()
        desc_size = block_descriptor.sizeof()

        descriptor = await self.symbols.malloc(desc_size)
        await descriptor.poke(block_descriptor.build({"reserved": 0, "size": block_size}))

        block = await self.symbols.malloc(block_size)
        await block.poke(
            block_literal.build({
                "isa": await self.symbols._NSConcreteGlobalBlock.resolve(),
                "flags": BLOCK_IS_GLOBAL,
                "reserved": 0,
                "invoke": await self.symbols.getpid.resolve(),
                "descriptor": descriptor,
            }),
        )

        return block

    async def listdir(self, path: str | PurePath) -> list[ProtocolDirent]:
        """get an address for a stub block containing nothing"""
        entries: list[ProtocolDirent] = []
        try:
            ret = await self.rpc_call(MsgId.REQ_LIST_DIR, path=str(path))
        except ServerResponseError:
            await self.raise_errno_exception(f"failed to listdir: {path}")

        for entry in ret.dir_entries:
            lstat = ProtocolDitentStat(
                errno=entry.lstat.errno1,
                st_blocks=entry.lstat.st_blocks,
                st_blksize=entry.lstat.st_blksize,
                st_atime=entry.lstat.st_atime1,
                st_ctime=entry.lstat.st_ctime1,
                st_mtime=entry.lstat.st_mtime1,
                st_nlink=entry.lstat.st_nlink,
                st_mode=entry.lstat.st_mode,
                st_rdev=entry.lstat.st_rdev,
                st_size=entry.lstat.st_size,
                st_dev=entry.lstat.st_dev,
                st_gid=entry.lstat.st_gid,
                st_ino=entry.lstat.st_ino,
                st_uid=entry.lstat.st_uid,
            )
            stat = ProtocolDitentStat(
                errno=entry.stat.errno1,
                st_blocks=entry.stat.st_blocks,
                st_blksize=entry.stat.st_blksize,
                st_atime=entry.stat.st_atime1,
                st_ctime=entry.stat.st_ctime1,
                st_mtime=entry.stat.st_mtime1,
                st_nlink=entry.stat.st_nlink,
                st_mode=entry.stat.st_mode,
                st_rdev=entry.stat.st_rdev,
                st_size=entry.stat.st_size,
                st_dev=entry.stat.st_dev,
                st_gid=entry.stat.st_gid,
                st_ino=entry.stat.st_ino,
                st_uid=entry.stat.st_uid,
            )
            entries.append(
                ProtocolDirent(
                    d_inode=entry.lstat.st_ino,
                    d_type=entry.d_type,
                    d_name=entry.d_name,
                    lstat=lstat,
                    stat=stat,
                )
            )
        return entries

    async def spawn(
        self,
        argv: list[str] | None = None,
        envp: list[str] | None = None,
        stdin: StrOrIO = sys.stdin,
        stdout=sys.stdout,
        raw_tty=False,
        background=False,
    ) -> SpawnResult:
        """
        spawn a new process and forward its stdin, stdout & stderr

        :param argv: argv of the process to be executed
        :param envp: envp of the process to be executed
        :param stdin: either a file object to read from OR a string
        :param stdout: a file object to write both stdout and stderr to. None if background is requested
        :param raw_tty: should enable raw tty mode
        :param background: should execute process in background
        :return: a SpawnResult. error is None if background is requested
        """
        if argv is None:
            argv = self.DEFAULT_ARGV

        if envp is None:
            envp = self.DEFAULT_ENVP

        async with self._acquire_protocol_lock():
            pid = await self._execute(argv, envp, background=background)
            self._logger.info(f"shell process started as pid: {pid}")

            if background:
                return SpawnResult(error=None, pid=pid, stdout=None)

            if raw_tty:
                self._prepare_terminal()
            try:
                error = await self.enter_pty_mode(stdin, stdout)
            except Exception:
                # this is important to really catch every exception here, even exceptions not inheriting from Exception
                # so the controlling terminal will remain working with its previous settings
                if raw_tty:
                    self._restore_terminal()
                raise

        return SpawnResult(error=error, pid=pid, stdout=stdout)

    @abc.abstractmethod
    def symbol(self, symbol: int) -> SymbolT_co:
        """Get a symbol object from a given address"""

    async def get_errno(self) -> int:
        return await self.symbols.errno.getindex(0)

    async def set_errno(self, value: int) -> None:
        await self.symbols.errno.setindex(0, value)

    async def get_last_error(self) -> str:
        """get info about the last occurred error"""
        if not (errno := await self.get_errno()):
            return ""
        err_str_ptr = await self.symbols.strerror(errno)
        err_str = await err_str_ptr.peek_str()
        return f"[{errno}] {err_str}"

    async def environ(self) -> list[str]:
        result = []
        environ = await self.symbols.environ.getindex(0)
        i = 0
        while var_ptr := await environ.getindex(i):
            result.append(await var_ptr.peek_str())
            i += 1
        return result

    async def setenv(self, name: str, value: str) -> None:
        """set process environment variable"""
        await (await self.symbols.setenv.resolve()).call(name, value)

    async def getenv(self, name: str) -> str | None:
        """get process environment variable"""
        value = await self.symbols.getenv(name)
        if not isinstance(value, Symbol) or not value:
            return None
        return await value.peek_str()

    _cached_pid: int | None = None

    async def get_pid(self) -> int:
        if self._cached_pid is None:
            self._cached_pid = int(await self.symbols.getpid())

        return self._cached_pid

    async def pid(self) -> int:
        return await self.get_pid()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def safe_calloc(self, size: int) -> AsyncGenerator[SymbolT_co]:
        async with self.safe_malloc(size) as x:
            await x.poke(b"\x00" * size)
            yield x

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def safe_malloc(self, size: int) -> AsyncGenerator[SymbolT_co]:
        ptr = cast(SymbolT_co, await self.symbols.malloc(size))
        async with self.freeing(ptr) as x:
            yield x

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def freeing(self, symbol: SymbolT) -> AsyncGenerator[SymbolT]:
        try:
            yield symbol
        finally:
            if symbol:
                await self.symbols.free(symbol)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        try:
            await self.rpc_call(MsgId.REQ_CLOSE_CLIENT)
        finally:
            self.notifier.notify(ClientEvent.TERMINATED, self.id)
            self._bridge.close()

    async def _execute(self, argv: list[str], envp: list[str], background=False) -> int:
        try:
            return (await self.rpc_call(MsgId.REQ_EXEC, background=background, argv=argv, envp=envp)).pid
        except ServerResponseError as e:
            raise SpawnError(f"failed to spawn: {argv}") from e

    async def enter_pty_mode(self, stdin=sys.stdin, stdout=sys.stdout):
        # the socket must be non-blocking for using select()
        sock = self._bridge.sock.raw_socket
        blocking = sock.getblocking()
        sock.setblocking(False)
        exit_code = None
        try:
            fds = []
            if hasattr(stdin, "fileno"):
                fds.append(stdin)
            else:
                data = stdin
                if isinstance(data, str):
                    data = data.encode()
                sock.sendall(cast(Buffer, data))
            fds.append(sock)

            running = True
            while running:
                rlist, _, _ = select(fds, [], [])
                for fd in rlist:
                    if fd == stdin or (stdin is sys.stdin and fd == sys.stdin):
                        if stdin is sys.stdin:
                            buf = os.read(stdin.fileno(), ProtocolConstants.RPC_PTY_BUFFER_SIZE)
                        else:
                            buf = stdin.read(ProtocolConstants.RPC_PTY_BUFFER_SIZE)
                            if isinstance(buf, str):
                                buf = buf.encode()
                        if buf:
                            sock.sendall(buf)
                    elif fd == sock:
                        try:
                            response = await self._bridge.sock.rpc_msg_recv_pty()
                        except ConnectionResetError:
                            print("Bye. 👋")
                            running = False
                            break
                        msg_type = response.WhichOneof("type")
                        if msg_type == "buffer":
                            stdout.write(response.buffer.decode())
                            if hasattr(stdout, "flush"):
                                stdout.flush()
                        elif msg_type == "exit_code":
                            exit_code = response.exit_code
                            running = False
                            break
        finally:
            sock.setblocking(blocking)
        return exit_code

    def _restore_terminal(self) -> None:
        if not tty_support:
            return
        assert self._old_settings is not None
        termios.tcsetattr(sys.stdin.fileno(), termios.TCSADRAIN, self._old_settings)  # pyright: ignore[reportPossiblyUnboundVariable]

    def _prepare_terminal(self):
        if not tty_support:
            return
        fd = sys.stdin
        self._old_settings = termios.tcgetattr(fd)  # pyright: ignore[reportPossiblyUnboundVariable]
        tty.setraw(fd)  # pyright: ignore[reportPossiblyUnboundVariable]

    async def raise_errno_exception(self, message: str):
        message += f" ({await self.get_last_error()})"
        exceptions = {
            EPERM: RpcPermissionError,
            ENOENT: RpcFileNotFoundError,
            EEXIST: RpcFileExistsError,
            EISDIR: RpcIsADirectoryError,
            ENOTDIR: RpcNotADirectoryError,
            EPIPE: RpcBrokenPipeError,
            ENOTEMPTY: RpcNotEmptyError,
            EAGAIN: RpcResourceTemporarilyUnavailableError,
            ECONNREFUSED: RpcConnectionRefusedError,
        }
        exception = exceptions.get(await self.get_errno())
        if exception:
            raise exception(message)
        raise BadReturnValueError(message)

    def capture_fd(self, fd: int, sock_buf_size: int | None = None) -> CaptureFD[SymbolT_co]:
        """
        Get a context manager, capturing output to `fd`. Read from it using the `read()` method

        sock_buf_size is required for captures above 6KB, as any write above this value would block until a read is performed.

        :param fd: FD to capture
        :param sock_buf_size: Buffer size for the capture socket, if not specified, default value is used.
        :return: CaptureFD object
        """
        return CaptureFD(self, fd, sock_buf_size)

    async def last_error(self) -> str:
        return await self.get_last_error()

    def shell(self) -> None:
        from xonsh.built_ins import XSH
        from xonsh.main import main as xonsh_main

        self._logger.disabled = True

        args = ["--rc"]
        args.append(str((Path(__file__).parent / "xonshrc.py").absolute()))

        XSH.ctx["_client_to_reuse"] = self

        try:
            logging.getLogger("parso.python.diff").disabled = True
            logging.getLogger("parso.cache").disabled = True
            logging.getLogger("asyncio").disabled = True
            xonsh_main(args)
        except SystemExit:
            self._logger.disabled = False

    async def __aenter__(self) -> Self:
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) -> None:
        await self.close()

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        pid = self._cached_pid if self._cached_pid is not None else "?"
        progname = self._cached_progname if self._cached_progname is not None else "?"
        return f"<{self.__class__.__name__}: {pid} | {progname}>"
```

### get_progname

```
get_progname() -> str
```

get the program name from remote

Source code in `src/rpcclient/rpcclient/core/client.py`

```
async def get_progname(self) -> str:
    """get the program name from remote"""
    if self._cached_progname is None:
        # bugfix https://github.com/doronz88/rpc-project/issues/405
        # Default Linux libraries don't expose `getprogname()`, so instead we use the `__progname` global symbol.
        # Tested on both macOS and Ubuntu.
        self._cached_progname = await (await self.symbols["__progname"].getindex(0)).peek_str()

    return self._cached_progname
```

### call

```
call(address: int, argv: Iterable[RemoteCallArg] = (), return_float64: bool = False, return_float32: bool = False, return_raw: bool = False, va_list_index: int | None = None) -> float | SymbolT_co | Any
```

call a remote function and retrieve its return value as a Symbol object

Source code in `src/rpcclient/rpcclient/core/client.py`

```
@null_pointer_guard
async def call(
    self,
    address: int,
    argv: Iterable[RemoteCallArg] = (),
    return_float64: bool = False,
    return_float32: bool = False,
    return_raw: bool = False,
    va_list_index: int | None = None,
) -> float | SymbolT_co | Any:
    """call a remote function and retrieve its return value as a Symbol object"""
    if va_list_index is None:
        va_list_index = 0xFFFF

    args: list[Argument] = []
    for arg in argv:
        if isinstance(arg, LazySymbol):
            arg = int(await arg.resolve())

        if isinstance(arg, float):
            args.append(Argument(v_double=arg))
        elif isinstance(arg, str):
            args.append(Argument(v_str=arg))
        elif isinstance(arg, int):
            args.append(Argument(v_int=ctypes.c_uint64(arg).value))
        elif isinstance(arg, bytes):
            args.append(Argument(v_bytes=arg))
        elif isinstance(arg, Enum):
            args.append(Argument(v_int=ctypes.c_uint64(arg.value).value))
        elif isinstance(arg, PurePath):
            args.append(Argument(v_str=str(arg)))
        else:
            assert_never(arg)
            raise ArgumentError(f"Can't serialize object of type {type(arg).__name__}")

    ret = await self.rpc_call(MsgId.REQ_CALL, address=address, va_list_index=va_list_index, argv=args)
    if ret.HasField("arm_registers"):
        d0 = ret.arm_registers.d0
        if return_float32:
            return ctypes.c_float(d0).value
        if return_float64:
            return d0
        if return_raw:
            return ret.arm_registers
        return self.symbol(ret.arm_registers.x0)
    return self.symbol(ret.return_value)
```

async def listdir(self, path: str | PurePath) -> list[ProtocolDirent]:

### spawn

```
spawn(argv: list[str] | None = None, envp: list[str] | None = None, stdin: StrOrIO = sys.stdin, stdout=sys.stdout, raw_tty=False, background=False) -> SpawnResult
```

spawn a new process and forward its stdin, stdout & stderr

Parameters:

| Name         | Type        | Description                                                                       | Default                            |
| ------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `argv`       | \`list[str] | None\`                                                                            | argv of the process to be executed |
| `envp`       | \`list[str] | None\`                                                                            | envp of the process to be executed |
| `stdin`      | `StrOrIO`   | either a file object to read from OR a string                                     | `stdin`                            |
| `stdout`     |             | a file object to write both stdout and stderr to. None if background is requested | `stdout`                           |
| `raw_tty`    |             | should enable raw tty mode                                                        | `False`                            |
| `background` |             | should execute process in background                                              | `False`                            |

Returns:

| Type          | Description                                             |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SpawnResult` | a SpawnResult. error is None if background is requested |

Source code in `src/rpcclient/rpcclient/core/client.py`

```
async def spawn(
    self,
    argv: list[str] | None = None,
    envp: list[str] | None = None,
    stdin: StrOrIO = sys.stdin,
    stdout=sys.stdout,
    raw_tty=False,
    background=False,
) -> SpawnResult:
    """
    spawn a new process and forward its stdin, stdout & stderr

    :param argv: argv of the process to be executed
    :param envp: envp of the process to be executed
    :param stdin: either a file object to read from OR a string
    :param stdout: a file object to write both stdout and stderr to. None if background is requested
    :param raw_tty: should enable raw tty mode
    :param background: should execute process in background
    :return: a SpawnResult. error is None if background is requested
    """
    if argv is None:
        argv = self.DEFAULT_ARGV

    if envp is None:
        envp = self.DEFAULT_ENVP

    async with self._acquire_protocol_lock():
        pid = await self._execute(argv, envp, background=background)
        self._logger.info(f"shell process started as pid: {pid}")

        if background:
            return SpawnResult(error=None, pid=pid, stdout=None)

        if raw_tty:
            self._prepare_terminal()
        try:
            error = await self.enter_pty_mode(stdin, stdout)
        except Exception:
            # this is important to really catch every exception here, even exceptions not inheriting from Exception
            # so the controlling terminal will remain working with its previous settings
            if raw_tty:
                self._restore_terminal()
            raise

    return SpawnResult(error=error, pid=pid, stdout=stdout)
```

### symbol

```
symbol(symbol: int) -> SymbolT_co
```

Get a symbol object from a given address

```
async def get_last_error(self) -> str:
    """get info about the last occurred error"""
    if not (errno := await self.get_errno()):
        return ""
    err_str_ptr = await self.symbols.strerror(errno)
    err_str = await err_str_ptr.peek_str()
    return f"[{errno}] {err_str}"
```

async def getenv(self, name: str) -> str | None:
    """get process environment variable"""
    value = await self.symbols.getenv(name)
    if not isinstance(value, Symbol) or not value:
        return None
    return await value.peek_str()

### capture_fd

```
capture_fd(fd: int, sock_buf_size: int | None = None) -> CaptureFD[SymbolT_co]
```

Get a context manager, capturing output to `fd`. Read from it using the `read()` method

sock_buf_size is required for captures above 6KB, as any write above this value would block until a read is performed.

Parameters:

| Name            | Type  | Description   | Default                                                                      |
| --------------- | ----- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fd`            | `int` | FD to capture | *required*                                                                   |
| `sock_buf_size` | \`int | None\`        | Buffer size for the capture socket, if not specified, default value is used. |

Returns:

| Type                    | Description      |
| ----------------------- | ---------------- |
| `CaptureFD[SymbolT_co]` | CaptureFD object |

Source code in `src/rpcclient/rpcclient/core/client.py`

```
def capture_fd(self, fd: int, sock_buf_size: int | None = None) -> CaptureFD[SymbolT_co]:
    """
    Get a context manager, capturing output to `fd`. Read from it using the `read()` method

    sock_buf_size is required for captures above 6KB, as any write above this value would block until a read is performed.

    :param fd: FD to capture
    :param sock_buf_size: Buffer size for the capture socket, if not specified, default value is used.
    :return: CaptureFD object
    """
    return CaptureFD(self, fd, sock_buf_size)
```

### DirEntry

Bases: `ClientBound[ClientT_co]`

Source code in `src/rpcclient/rpcclient/core/subsystems/fs.py`

```
class DirEntry(ClientBound[ClientT_co]):
    def __init__(self, path, entry, client: ClientT_co) -> None:
        self._path = path
        self._entry = entry
        self._client = client
        self._stat = None

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return self._entry.d_name

    @property
    def path(self) -> str:
        return posixpath.join(self._path, self.name)

    def inode(self):
        """Return inode of the entry; cached per entry."""
        return self._entry.d_ino

    async def is_dir(self, *, follow_symlinks=True) -> bool:
        """Return True if the entry is a directory; cached per entry."""
        return await self._test_mode(follow_symlinks, S_IFDIR)

    async def is_file(self, *, follow_symlinks: bool = True):
        """Return True if the entry is a file; cached per entry."""
        return await self._test_mode(follow_symlinks, S_IFREG)

    async def is_symlink(self) -> bool:
        """Return True if the entry is a symbolic link; cached per entry."""
        if self._entry.d_type != DT_UNKNOWN:
            return self._entry.d_type == DT_LNK
        else:
            return await self._test_mode(False, S_IFLNK)

    async def stat(self, *, follow_symlinks: bool = True):
        """Return stat_result object for the entry; cached per entry."""
        if not follow_symlinks:
            return await self._get_lstat()
        if self._stat is None:
            if await self.is_symlink():
                self._stat = await self._fetch_stat(True)
            else:
                self._stat = await self._get_lstat()
        return self._stat

    async def _test_mode(self, follow_symlinks, mode) -> bool:
        is_symlink = self._entry.d_type == DT_LNK
        need_stat = self._entry.d_type == DT_UNKNOWN or (follow_symlinks and is_symlink)
        if not need_stat:
            d_types = {S_IFLNK: DT_LNK, S_IFDIR: DT_DIR, S_IFREG: DT_REG}
            return self._entry.d_type == d_types[mode]
        else:
            st_mode = (await self.stat(follow_symlinks=follow_symlinks)).st_mode
            if not st_mode:
                await self._client.raise_errno_exception(f"failed to stat(): {self.path}")
            return (st_mode & S_IFMT) == mode

    @cached_async_method
    async def _get_lstat(self):
        return await self._fetch_stat(False)

    async def _fetch_stat(self, follow_symlinks):
        result = self._entry.stat
        if not follow_symlinks:
            result = self._entry.lstat

        if result.errno != 0:
            await self._client.set_errno(result.errno)
            await self._client.raise_errno_exception(f"failed to stat: {self._entry.d_name}")
        return result

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<{self.__class__.__name__} name={self.name!r}>"
```
